text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic met directors of the leading construction companies on Monday. He said that the great project of building a trans-Yugoslav highway would certainly be a major contribution to speeding up country's economic development.
- Yugoslavia and Ukraine signed agreement on military cooperation.
- Yugoslav businessmen say high interest rates which are the main obstacle to boosting of exports and production must be removed.

- Director of the federal statistics office said that December inflation will be about two percent because of the rise of tobacco and electricity prices. Annual inflation will be about 58 percent over December last year, he said.
- About 150,000 farmers in Serbia will receive first part of their August pension on Tuesday with an average amount of 116 dinars ($22).
- Yugoslav banks began regular payment of German pensions.
- Federal parliament chamber of citizens' constitutive session after November 3 elections to be held on Tuesday.
- Montenegrin government said it expected 29 percent gross domestic product growth this year against projected 23 percent.
- Most of Belgrade theaters will be closed on Tuesday in protest over "violation of citizens rights, constitution and democratic principles".
- Dejan Bulatovic, who was arrested on Sunday during opposition protests in Belgrade, was transfered to emergency clinic for medical examination.
- U.N. special envoy for human rights Elisabeth Rehn in a letter to Serbian President Slobodan MIlosevic demanded freedom of press.
- About 15,000 people protested over violation of basic human rights in southern Serbian town of Nis on Monday.
- Belgrade public transport independent union called for strike over unpaid wages.
- About 1,000 people protested in eastern Serbian town of Negotin on Monday in support of Belgrade demonstrators.
